paper.title: Algorithm 886: Padua2D: Lagrange interpolation at Padua points on bivariate domains
paper.url: https://doi.org/10.1145/1391989.1391994 (open pre-publication draft, titled 'Algorithm xxx: Padua2D', read at https://www.math.unipd.it/~demarchi/papers/padua2d.pdf, sha256 be72d8c9e04b3b9aefa92b078747a273676b66cfb198f53cb7bf271bd425b23a)

code.note: Fortran 77 under Fortran/Dp/Src (padua2.f, pdpts.f, pd2val.f, cheb.f, and a BLAS subset in Src/blas). Three drivers in Fortran/Dp/Drivers: drvrec.f (square, DEG = 60, FTYPE = 1 is the Franke function F1, 100 x 100 target grid). The shipped Results/ files are not used for this claim: their intftg.dat coordinates do not match the target grid written by the shipped drvrec.f (only 100 of 10000 points coincide), so they are not a usable oracle.

claim.location: Section 3.3 (Error estimates), Table I: 'True' normalized error of interpolation at Padua points for the classical Franke test suite (taken from Caliari et al. 2007), row degree n = 60, column F1: 2E-11. The text says all errors are normalized to the maximum deviation of the function from its mean and the true errors are computed on a 100 x 100 uniform control grid. The read copy is the pre-publication draft; the published TOMS table may differ, and rerun must record which version it compared against.
claim.metric: Normalized true error of the interpolant L_n f at degree n = 60 for the Franke function F1 on the unit square [0,1]^2: max over a 100 x 100 uniform grid of |f - L_n f| divided by max |f - mean(f)| over the same grid (the driver's MAXERR / MAXDEV, with DEG = 60, NTG1 = 100, FTYPE = 1). The rerun may compile drvrec.f against the shipped sources and compute this quantity itself; it must not read a shipped output file as the answer.
claim.paper_value: 2E-11 (one significant figure, as printed in Table I)

values.name: normalized true error, F1, degree 60, square

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The paper prints one significant figure, so the printed value 2E-11 stands for any value in [1.5E-11, 2.5E-11]; tol_abs 5e-12 is exactly that half-unit interval. It does not cover the parenthesised estimate (3E-10 is an estimate, not this claim). Double-precision rounding at degree 60 is far below this scale, so the tolerance tests the algorithm and not the compiler.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 5 minutes (one driver run on 1326 Padua points and 10000 targets; no data files).
cost.data_size: None; the Franke function is analytic and the driver generates its grid.
cost.data_licence: Netlib TOMS code under the ACM licence of the archive; rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The Padua interpolant at degree 60 needs the Chebyshev-based coefficient computation and the PD2VAL evaluation to be run; the table value is a computed error on a 100 x 100 grid, not an input echo.
